decisions.rationale: All 212 comparators were reviewed. The two projection-trust comparators concern adjacent freshness and gate-selection contracts, but neither shares this GitHub projection gate's authority, lifecycle, identity inputs, and race boundary.

All comparators were considered. General mutation-transition and safe-point receipt gaps are adjacent, while this anchor specifically governs atomic GitHub prerequisite-version binding to remote dispatch and reconciliation.
Cross-surface diagnostics and event correlation are plausible neighbors, but they do not own the GitHub attribution envelope, its propagation matrix, or its seam semantics.
The related items also expose privacy or identity lifecycle gaps, but their records, consumers, retention boundaries, and failure consequences differ from GitHub usage and audit rows.
Generic mutation recovery and OAuth callback security are adjacent to browser-auth handoff, but neither is the confirmation-to-mutation transaction with rollback and provenance validation owned here.
The FileSafe retired bridge is a close structural analogue and the GitHub owner boundary is adjacent, but different retired authorities and product coverage prevent merge equivalence.

Daemon loss, child authority freshness, and SSH stability are related disconnect concerns, but use different authorities, state machines, outcomes, and recovery boundaries from remote-only Git execution.

OAuth callback lifecycle is adjacent authentication recovery, but it is not the device-flow polling backoff, rate-limit, expiry, cancellation, and restart-lease protocol. No comparator is merge-equivalent.

Credential snapshot lifecycle, GitHub ownership, and stable identity are adjacent, but none owns provider account-root isolation, sharing, eligibility, cooldown revalidation, and transactional import together.

These comparators touch revocation, credentials, OAuth, identity, or account disclosure, but the anchor's combined account authentication, registration, readiness, removal, and compensation lifecycle remains a distinct authority boundary.

The neighbors cover credential data, freshness, store outage, or stable identity separately; none shares the credential-route epoch, native token-store atomicity, rotating fetch, and failover lifecycle.

The listed permission and approval items are members or adjacent implementations of the broader concern, with different scope, state, or UI boundaries; umbrella/member structure is not merge equivalence.
Approval-card and recovery races are close neighbors, but the anchor uniquely governs primary/fallback surface handoff and single-decision authority across surfaces.

Blocked episode, action mapping, decision authority, and session-card races intersect the deny cascade, but none shares its reject-all atomic cascade, pending-set snapshot, scope-key comparison, and rollback semantics.

Related approval surfaces lack portions of the same UX state vocabulary, but this anchor owns the shared Slint/CLI reply-mapping and synchronization seam rather than any individual card or recovery control.

Path extraction, encoding, and shell identity are related untrusted-input seams, but none owns command-template expansion, filesystem containment, MCP compatibility, and failed-expansion behavior as one lifecycle.
These comparators govern cards, blocked actions, and recovery around approvals, but not the canonical permission reply labels, valid transitions, error mapping, replay, and cascade interaction.
Attachment blocking and visible recovery are adjacent composer experiences, while the anchor's input-preservation, blocker stacking, reconnect, focus, and stale-state lifecycle is distinct.

Concrete identity surfaces raise related privacy concerns, but the concept-only login/privacy fixture has no production auth authority or lifecycle and therefore cannot merge with that GUI-scope item.

Bulk deletion, transactional filesystem outcomes, and cleanup precedence are plausible destructive-lifecycle neighbors, but they are not the unspecified production semantics of this Remove affordance.
Shared accessible disabled controls and shell-level accessibility are related, but neither governs semantic roles and accessible names for the repeated interactive skill-row custom targets.
Exhaustive review of all 212 comparators found no plausible neighbor with the same masked-key concept-fixture and non-evidence boundary, and no merge-equivalent feature.
The neighbors each cover one privacy, credential, diagnostic, identity, or projection lifecycle seam; none owns the combined settings controls and enforcement authority described by the anchor.

Filesystem containment and boundary-test gaps are related, but this anchor concerns authority-bearing settings and broad tool/root-path controls rather than FileSafe's enforcement implementation or fixtures.

Vision-source permission and explicit policy authority are adjacent, but the protected retrieval resources, ask lifecycle, overrides, consumers, and enforcement evidence remain a distinct authority model.
Execution-context and identity-surface privacy lifecycles are neighboring data-governance concerns, but they do not own assistant-memory collection, retention, deletion, access, or user outcome.
After comparing every comparator, no feature plausibly governs the unnamed assistant-memory numeric parameters, their units, bounds, invalid states, and acceptance oracles.

Approved-command lifecycle, layered guard configuration, and pattern reload are related policy machinery, but differ from the shown blocklist path and comma-list parsing, precedence, refresh, enforcement, and audit contract.

GUI-to-runtime propagation and config projection lifecycle are adjacent, but the anchor concerns absent canonical command identity, schemas, consumer wiring, enforcement, and recovery for different controls.
Retired disabled-on-failure snippets share a non-authoritative lineage boundary, but they are not the local container executable-path fixtures excluded from acceptance evidence.

Cross-platform portability and installed-layout lookup are related to runtime discovery, but neither selects Docker versus Podman or owns compatibility, migration, offline, failure, and recovery rules.

Persistent approvals, authenticated controls, and permission authority are related, but this anchor's global/per-tool/pattern precedence and enforcement are only concept lineage and remain a distinct missing contract.
Approval and recovery controls are adjacent, but the anchor specifically requires Browser Permissions and restart/recovery affordances to gain concrete command identities or be retired.
SSH stability is a plausible neighboring surface, but it does not define the SSH port field's identity, valid range, default, privilege constraint, or validation oracle.

Credential lifecycle, SSH stability, store outage, and authority-domain separation are adjacent, but none owns the SSH authentication selector's source trust, fallback, prompting, host verification, and receipts.

FileSafe has parallel canonical-path and fail-closed enforcement features, but those are enforcement-layer authorities rather than the permission path-matching authority and therefore remain related, not merged.

Requested/effective FileSafe display and GUI permission authority are adjacent consumers, but the anchor owns layered rule precedence, downward inheritance, specificity, and effective-state disclosure across permission policy.
The comparators expose analogous filesystem TOCTOU and symlink races, but in worktree and FileSafe mutation authorities; this permission check-to-open binding remains a distinct state boundary.

Persistent command scope, exact approval identity, and web session approvals are plausible consumers, but none defines the canonical approval-scope key field set, serialization, normalization, versioning, privacy form, and equality vectors.

Credential data, stores, and GitHub authority boundaries are related, but PS-119's provider-route locator-only custody, proof metadata, snapshots, and redaction constitute a separate product contract.
Credential snapshots and stable identity lifecycles are adjacent, but neither resolves PS-119's internal contradiction between permitted account/profile references and forbidden account identifiers.
Web session approval races and GitHub host policy are neighboring host-scope concerns, but neither defines registrable-domain approval identity or prevents silent subdomain broadening.
Authority revocation and web session cards are related, but the anchor is the normative contradiction between promotion-to-allow and narrowing-only session-cache resolution.
Exhaustive review found no comparator that plausibly shares the malformed batch-webfetch declaration boundary, and no item matches its authority, schema failure, or outcome.

Authenticated destructive authority and safe-point receipts are adjacent safeguards, but external publication has its own non-bypassable exact remote-effect gate, ordered approvals, and partial-success recovery semantics.
GUI config propagation and FileSafe struct preservation are related schema consumers, but neither is the scalar-versus-table collision in canonical permission TOML and guard examples.
General authority revocation and persistent-command lifecycle are related, but the anchor is the specific omission of required rule_id from the durable-record acceptance oracle.
Revocation, UI data cleanup, projection trust, and config projection lifecycle are adjacent, but none owns stale persisted merged-permission invalidation for memory-only session approvals.
Canonical event and GUI permission authority items are related infrastructure, but the anchor specifically establishes provenance-aware effective permission rows and seglog audit visibility.
Restrictive and persistent guard defaults are adjacent posture definitions, but they do not resolve the two incompatible permission-system meanings assigned to Read-only.

CAS, general mutation transitions, and safe-point receipts are related safeguards, but this anchor's target-bound preflight, in-flight dedupe, runtime revalidation, and indeterminate remote reconciliation remain distinct.
Projection trust context is a plausible consumer of source provenance, but it does not own the closed snapshot-source enum or its inability to represent required clamps and precedence sources.
Blocked payload spelling and action mapping are neighboring schema consistency issues, but neither is the collision among blocked-family, recovery-state, and closed reason-code vocabularies.

Blocked transition, authority freshness, safe-point, and action-mapping items are adjacent, but the approval-resolution event-to-scheduler wakeup transaction, ordering, durability, and crash recovery are distinct.
The comparators share missing executable-oracle quality defects, but concern different FileManager/FileSafe behaviors and tests; shared audit vocabulary is not product-feature equivalence.

Dispatch, transport, blocked-decision, and GUI policy boundaries are related consumers, but the anchor is the permission approval authority's propagation across actor, lane, runtime, remote-effect, provider, GUI, and trust consumers; adjacency and consumer structure do not merge.
